title: bug: chat_read with an explicit sinceId rewrites the caller's chat cursors: a channel peek rewinds the cursor (chat_wait re-delivers handled messages) and an all-channel peek jumps other channels past unread mentions
description:
Filed by architect-1dd28c7c from the daemon/proxy defect hunt (task-8f18d6fa).

PROBLEM
moe.chat_read (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatRead.ts) writes the caller's per-channel chatCursors and clears unread whenever workerId is present. That includes reads that pass an explicit sinceId. moe-proxy injects workerId into every chat_read a seat makes (injectWorkerId in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts exempts only get_activity_log), so no seat can peek at older messages without moving its cursor. state/workerStore.ts updateWorkerCursors merges the new id unconditionally.
1. Channel read with a sinceId older than the stored cursor: the cursor is set to the last message of that page, so it moves backwards. The next cursor-mode chat_read and the next chat_wait both re-deliver everything after it. Seen live on 2026-11-03: after a chat_read peek at msg-45ae900d (12:30Z), the governor's 13:10Z chat_wait re-sent about 10 messages it had already handled.
2. All-channel read (no channel) with an explicit sinceId: the id is applied to every channel. A channel that does not hold it trips getMessages' expired-cursor fallback (state/chatStore.ts) and returns its newest window. That channel's cursor then jumps to its newest message and its unread count is cleared, so the messages between the old cursor and that window are never delivered, direct mentions included. util/chatBacklog.ts collectChatBacklog already guards this case for chat_wait ("An explicit catch-up id belongs to ONE channel"); chat_read does not. This is distinct from the archived task-a0973700 fix, which covers fetched-but-omitted messages in all-channel mode.
3. An explicit sinceId ahead of the stored cursor skips the messages in between the same way.

EVIDENCE: repro on HEAD 99cae90a (a descendant of 1558f141), run in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout with Linux node_modules. Repro file and full output: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/zzReproCursor.test.ts and /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/repro-output-99cae90a.txt. To re-run, copy the test into a snapshot's packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/.
Command: cd <snapshot>/packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/zzReproCursor.test.ts
Observed:
REPRO first read      : m1,m2,m3,m4,m5,m6 | stored cursor = m6
REPRO peek sinceId=m1 : m2 | stored cursor = m2 (REWOUND from m6)
REPRO next plain read : m3,m4,m5,m6 (already delivered by the first read)
REPRO chat_wait after a second peek: true m3,m4,m5,m6
REPRO2 #workers read            : w1,w2,w3,w4,w5 | cursor w5
REPRO2 unread before            : {"chan-51896eb3...":1}   (w7 mentions the reader)
REPRO2 all-channel sinceId=g1   : w11,w12,w13,w14,w15,w16,w17,w18,w19,w20
REPRO2 #workers cursor now      : w20
REPRO2 unread after             : {}
REPRO2 next #workers plain read : []   (w6..w10, including the w7 mention, never delivered)
Tests 2 failed (2)

FIX DIRECTION
Make an explicit-sinceId chat_read a peek: it returns the page but writes no cursor and clears no unread count. Cursor-mode reads (workerId without sinceId, the only form both wrappers use) keep advancing exactly as today. In all-channel mode, apply the explicit id only to the channel that holds it (state.messageExistsInChannel, as collectChatBacklog does); other channels read from the caller's stored cursor. Update the tool description string in chatRead.ts to say a sinceId read does not move cursors. Keep the existing error handling for unknown channels and bad limits.
Out of scope:
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md: task-0c78c290 holds it at filing. Its chat_read notes can follow in a docs pass.
- chat_wait's explicit-sinceId catch-up.
- chatStore's 1 MB tail window.
Files: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatRead.ts, plus one new test file (e.g. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatRead.cursor.test.ts).
definitionOfDone: A chat_read with workerId and an explicit sinceId leaves the caller's stored chatCursors and unread counts unchanged, in channel and all-channel mode. A vitest case seeds a cursor at m6, peeks with sinceId=m1 and limit 1, and asserts the stored cursor is still m6 and that the next cursor-mode chat_read returns no messages.

An all-channel chat_read with an explicit sinceId applies the id only to the channel that holds it. A vitest case puts an unread direct mention in another channel past its stored cursor, and asserts that channel's cursor and unread count are unchanged and its next cursor-mode read still returns the mention.

Cursor-mode reads (workerId, no sinceId) still advance cursors and clear unread as before: tools/chatBudgets.test.ts, chatChannelRef.test.ts, chatSystemFeed.test.ts and chatWait.test.ts pass unchanged, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (RED). Create packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatRead.cursor.test.ts using ToolTestHarness (tools/toolTestHarness.ts). In beforeEach: h.init(); h.setupMoeFolder(); h.createWorker for a READER seat and a PEER seat BEFORE `await h.state.load()` (as completeStep.test.ts does); then take the general and workers channel ids from h.state.getChannels(). Post with h.state.sendMessage({ channel, sender: PEER, content }), read through chatReadTool(h.state).handler, and inspect h.state.getWorker(READER).chatCursors and h.state.getUnreadSummary(READER). A direct mention of the reader is content built at runtime as an at-sign plus the READER id; that is what raises its unread count. Table-drive where it is natural, and keep the file at or under about 180 lines.

Cases:
(1) DoD 1, channel peek keeps the cursor. Post m1..m6 in general. A cursor-mode read (workerId, no sinceId, limit 10) returns all six and stores m6. Then peek with sinceId m1 and limit 1: the page is [m2] and the response cursor is m2, but the stored cursor is still m6. The next cursor-mode read returns []. A chat_wait on general for the reader with timeoutMs 1000 (its floor) then returns hasMessage false: nothing is re-delivered.
(2) A peek leaves unread untouched. After (1)'s cursor read, the peer posts m7, which mentions the reader, so unread for general is 1. A peek with sinceId m1 and limit 50 includes m7 in the page, while unread for general stays 1 and the cursor stays m6. The next cursor-mode read then returns exactly [m7], stores m7 and clears the general unread count. That is cursor mode unchanged.
(3) A peek ahead of the cursor skips nothing. Post m1, m2 and read in cursor mode (cursor m2). Post m3..m6. A peek with sinceId m4 returns [m5, m6] and the cursor stays m2. The next cursor-mode read returns [m3, m4, m5, m6].
(4) DoD 2, an all-channel peek applies the id only to its channel. Post w1..w5 in workers and read workers in cursor mode (cursor w5). Post w6..w20, where w7 mentions the reader (workers unread 1), then g1 and g2 in general. An all-channel read with workerId, sinceId g1 and limit 50 (no channel) returns a page whose workers messages are exactly w6..w20 in order (read from the stored cursor, not the newest window) and whose general messages are exactly [g2]. Filter the page by channel, because equal millisecond timestamps make the cross-channel order unstable. Afterwards: the workers cursor is still w5, no general cursor was written, and the workers unread count is still 1. A cursor-mode workers read with limit 50 then returns w6..w20, including the w7 mention.
(5) An anonymous all-channel peek is unchanged. The same messages, no workerId, sinceId g1 and limit 50: the workers part is its newest window, w1..w20.
(6) chatReadTool(h.state).description and its inputSchema sinceId description both say a sinceId read is a peek that moves no cursor. Use a case-insensitive regex on 'peek' and on 'cursor'.

Run it RED against the unmodified chatRead.ts in a snapshot outside the shared checkout. Use the step-4 recipe, but run only this file; never npm in the shared checkout (rail). Keep the failing lines for the completion summary: (1), (2), (3), (4) and (6) must fail, and (5) passes.
Error handling in the test: no try/catch around a tool call; a thrown tool error fails the case.

(1) cursor expected m6 got m2; (2) post-peek unread expected 1 got 0 (line 76, after pre-peek unread==1 passed); (3) cursor rewound; (4) workers page was w1..w20 newest window not w6..w20; (6) description lacks 'peek'. (5) anonymous all-channel peek passes as planned.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatRead.ts, one concern: a read with an explicit sinceId is a peek.
(a) Near the top of the handler, set `const explicitSinceId = params.sinceId || undefined;`, so an empty string keeps today's cursor mode, then `const peek = explicitSinceId !== undefined;`. Comment why: a peek pages from that id but writes no stored cursor and clears no unread count. Otherwise it rewinds the cursor chat_wait drains from, or skips unread messages.
(b) Channel mode is unchanged. It reads from the explicit id, else (with workerId) the stored cursor, else the newest window.
(c) All-channel mode: inside the per-channel loop, use the explicit id only for a channel that holds it, else the caller's stored cursor for that channel (undefined without a workerId): `explicitSinceId && state.messageExistsInChannel(ch.id, explicitSinceId) ? explicitSinceId : existingCursors[ch.id]`. existingCursors stays {} without a workerId, so an anonymous read keeps today's newest-window behavior. Add a comment citing collectChatBacklog's same rule (util/chatBacklog.ts ~171): an id applied to a channel that does not hold it trips getMessages' expired-cursor fallback (state/chatStore.ts ~325) and returns that channel's newest window. messageExistsInChannel reads the same bounded 1 MB tail as getMessages, so the two agree.
(d) Guard BOTH the updateWorkerCursors block and the clearUnread block with `!peek`. The response shape (messages, cursor = the page's last id, truncated, hint), the response-size trim and touchWorker stay exactly as they are.
(e) The tool description gets one sentence: a read with sinceId is a peek that moves no stored cursor or unread count. In all-channel mode the id applies only to the channel that holds it, and the other channels read from the caller's stored cursor. Omit sinceId to read from and advance your cursor. The sinceId property description says the same in a few words.
Error handling: keep the existing refusals (invalid limit or maxContentChars, an unknown channel via notFound) byte-identical. messageExistsInChannel already returns false on an unreadable file, so a channel that cannot be checked falls back to the stored cursor and never throws. Done when the step-1 file passes in the snapshot.
implementationPlan.note: chatRead.ts: explicitSinceId = params.sinceId || undefined; peek = explicitSinceId !== undefined; all-channel loop applies the id only to a channel that holds it (state.messageExistsInChannel), else existingCursors[ch.id]; updateWorkerCursors and clearUnread blocks guarded with !peek; description and sinceId property say a sinceId read is a peek. Existing refusals untouched. Snapshot run of chatRead.cursor.test.ts: 6 passed (6).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.chat_read with an explicit (non-empty) sinceId becomes a peek. It returns the page after that id, but never writes the caller's stored chatCursors and never clears an unread count, in channel and all-channel mode alike. In all-channel mode the explicit id applies only to the channel that holds it, the rule collectChatBacklog already applies: every other channel reads from the caller's stored cursor, or its newest window when there is no workerId. Cursor-mode reads (workerId without sinceId), the only form the wrappers and wait_for_task's hint use, keep advancing cursors and clearing unread exactly as today. This error handling keeps every existing refusal (bad limit or maxContentChars, an unknown channel) unchanged, and a test pins each behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Stored cursor m6, then a peek with sinceId m1 and limit 1: the page is [m2] and the stored cursor stays m6. The next cursor-mode read returns [], and chat_wait re-delivers nothing.
A peek leaves a channel's unread count unchanged; the next cursor-mode read returns the mention and clears the count.
A peek ahead of the cursor skips nothing for the next cursor-mode read.

An all-channel peek with an id from general reads workers from its stored cursor. It leaves workers' cursor and unread count unchanged, and the next cursor-mode workers read still returns the unread direct mention.
chatBudgets, chatChannelRef, chatSystemFeed, chatWait, joinTeam.notification and completeStep pass unchanged in a snapshot outside the shared checkout, and tsc --noEmit is clean.
invariants: Cursor-mode chat_read (workerId, no sinceId) behaves byte-for-byte as before.
A read without workerId behaves as before, the all-channel newest-window fallback for an id a channel does not hold included.
The chat_read response shape is unchanged: messages, cursor, truncated, hint.
No change to chat_wait, chatStore, workerStore or the proxy's workerId injection.
compatibility: A request with sinceId keeps returning the same page and cursor field. Only the stored-cursor and unread side effects change, which is the fix.
An empty-string sinceId still means cursor mode.

sourceAssumptions: tools/chatRead.ts writes updateWorkerCursors and clearUnread whenever workerId is set and the page is non-empty, sinceId or not. In all-channel mode it applies params.sinceId to every channel.
state/chatStore.ts getMessages falls back to the newest window when sinceId is not in the channel's bounded 1 MB tail. messageExistsInChannel scans the same tail and returns false on any read error.
util/chatBacklog.ts collectChatBacklog (~171) already applies an explicit catch-up id only to the channel that holds it.

moe-proxy injectWorkerId adds workerId to every chat_read. Both wrappers' chat_read calls pass channel and workerId only (moe-agent.sh ~9571/~9943, moe-agent.ps1 ~9254/~9529). The plugins read chat through WebSocketServer, which calls state.getMessages directly (~1078), not this tool.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Make a sinceId read never move the cursor backwards but still advance it forward: rejected, because a forward peek past unread messages (bug item 3) would still skip them. A peek has to write nothing. (2) Stop the proxy from injecting workerId into chat_read: rejected. workerId still feeds touchWorker activity and the stored-cursor fallback for other channels, and the proxy is out of scope. (3) Validate sinceId as a non-empty string the way chat_wait does: rejected as an API change; an empty string keeps meaning cursor mode.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: chat_read has one handler for both modes. Cursor writes happen in a single updateWorkerCursors block and unread clears in a single clearUnread block, both after the response-size trim, so one `!peek` guard on each covers every mode. Only collectChatBacklog (chat_wait) already guards an explicit id per channel. The plugins never call this tool.
planningNotes.risks: An all-channel peek now does one extra bounded tail read per channel. Equal millisecond timestamps make cross-channel page order unstable, so tests filter by channel. chatWait's minimum timeout is 1000 ms, so case (1) costs about 1 s. Nothing else depends on sinceId reads moving the cursor: the wrappers, wait_for_task's nextAction and every existing test use cursor mode.
